A DOG'S PERFECT CHRISTMAS officially releases tomorrow, November 4, on Netflix, bringing a brand new heartwarming holiday movie starring Dennis Quaid and Mary Steenburgen.

Based on the novel by W. Bruce Cameron, the bestselling author behind A DOG'S PURPOSE, the film follows a family whose Christmas plans fall apart after an unexpected medical emergency changes everything.

At the center of the story is Winstead, a loyal basset hound who tries to bring his struggling family back together before Christmas Eve, proving that sometimes the smallest members of a household can make the biggest difference.

The movie also stars Milo Ventimiglia, Jennifer Tilly, and Brooke Lena Johnson, with Thomas Haden Church providing the voice of Winstead. It marks another emotional dog-centered story from the author who brought audiences A DOG'S PURPOSE and A DOG'S JOURNEY.

Christmas movies are officially making their way back to Netflix, and A DOG'S PERFECT CHRISTMAS looks ready to deliver everything that makes the holidays special. Family, second chances, a little Christmas magic, and one very good dog holding everything together.

Netflix is once again testing a major redesign for its TV app. This new layout moves the main navigation menu back to the left-hand side of the screen, just months after the streamer rolled out a top-bar design globally. 

Beyond the sidebar, the test includes a layout that fits more titles on your screen at once, making it easier to scan through your watchlist. Video previews have also been moved to the top of the screen to free up space. This is currently only a test for select accounts, but it hints at where the Netflix experience is heading next.

“Chicago Fire” is airing its 300th episode. Taylor Kinney never thought he’d be here: wp.me/pc8uak-1lI43u

“I remember, going into Season 2 or 3, running into Mariska Hargitay. She had just got done negotiating her deal for season 16 or 17, and that was a whole other thing — it wasn’t even in my brain that something like that would be possible, let alone in the cards,” says Kinney, who has been on “Chicago Fire” since its start in 2012.

The episode is also an extremely emotional one, as it marks the last for Joe Miñoso’s Joe Cruz, who has also been on the show since the beginning. Kinney adds he had a “visceral, raw” reaction to filming the final Severide and Cruz scene:

“It’s one of those things that I’ll never forget. We spend a lot of time together, and at times, more than family. Starting out, these were 15- to 16-hour days, sometimes six days a week. Joe’s been my right-hand man for the past almost a decade, and there’s a lot of time spent looking someone in the eye, telling the truth. It’s just an intimate relationship. So to have a scene where the art imitates life and vice versa… it was raw, it was real, and it was honest. I cherish that moment, and that’ll be with me forever.”

An appeals court ruled that “The Pitt” is similar enough to “ER” to allow Michael Crichton’s widow to pursue a lawsuit over the Emmy-winning show.

The appeals court did dismiss a claim against key creators of the show — Noah Wyle, John Wells and R. Scott Gemmill — finding no evidence that they were aware they could be violating Crichton’s contractual rights.

“There are clear and numerous similarities between ‘The Pitt’ and ‘ER,” the court ruled, citing the emergency room setting, the fast pace, the medical jargon, the graphic depictions of injuries, and a young, incompetent doctor fresh from medical school. “We find the details here suffice for a prima facie case.”

नेपाली कांग्रेसका सहमहामन्त्री अजयबाबु शिवाकोटीलाई नेपाल प्रहरीको साइबर ब्युरोले बोलाएको छ। धार्मिक यात्राका लागि काठमाडौं बाहिर रहेका शिवाकोटीलाई फोनमार्फत ब्युरोमा उपस्थित हुन भनिएको हो।

शिवाकोटीले आफू साइबर ब्युरो जाने र काठमाडौं फर्किंदै गरेको बताएका छन्। बिहीबार बिहान सामाजिक सञ्जालमा प्रतिक्रिया दिँदै उनले सरकारको डर र भ्रमबाट विचलित नहुने उल्लेख गरेका छन्। उनले लेखेका छन्, ‘सरकार तिम्रो भय र पारेको भ्रमले विचलित हुन्न, प्रहरी लगाएर खोज्नु पर्दैन, काठमाडौं आउँदैछु।’

ब्युरो स्रोतका अनुसार पत्रकार रोशन खड्काले दिएको उजुरीका आधारमा शिवाकोटीलाई बोलाइएको हो। तर उजुरीमा उल्लेख भएका विषय र अनुसन्धानको विस्तृत विवरण सार्वजनिक भएको छैन।

शिवाकोटीले पछिल्ला दिनमा सामाजिक सञ्जालमार्फत सरकारले विधि र विधान मिचेर काम गरिरहेको तथा कांग्रेसलाई अनावश्यक विवादमा फसाउन खोजेको आरोप लगाउँदै आएका छन्।

सगरमाथा क्षेत्र पुगेपछि अस्ट्रेलियन क्रिकेटर डेभिड वार्नरले सेयर गरे मनमोहक हेलिकोप्टर भिडियो

नेपाल प्रिमियर लिग (एनपीएल) खेल्न नेपाल आएका अस्ट्रेलियन क्रिकेट स्टार डेभिड वार्नर हेलिकोप्टरमार्फत सगरमाथा क्षेत्र पुगेका छन्। उनले बुधबार साँझ आफ्नो आधिकारिक इन्स्टाग्राम अकाउन्टमा भ्रमणको मनमोहक भिडियो सार्वजनिक गरेका छन्। उनका इन्स्टाग्राममा १ करोड ३ लाखभन्दा बढी फलोअर्स छन्।

सगरमाथालाई आफ्नै आँखाले देख्नु अविश्वसनीय र जीवनकै अविस्मरणीय अनुभव भएको वार्नरले बताएका छन्। तस्बिर र भिडियोले हिमालको वास्तविक सुन्दरता देखाउन नसक्ने उल्लेख गर्दै उनले सगरमाथालाई आफ्नो क्रिकेट करिअरमा सामना गरेका तीव्र गतिका बलरभन्दा पनि कठिन प्रतिद्वन्द्वी भन्दै रमाइलो टिप्पणी गरेका छन्।

करिब १९ हजार फिट उचाइमा पुगेका वार्नरले त्यहाँको चिसो र पातलो हावाको अनुभव पनि सेयर गरेका छन्। उनलाई त्यहाँ बिस्तारै हिँड्न सुझाव दिइएको थियो। यसअघि उनले नेपालको प्राकृतिक सुन्दरता, आतिथ्य र नेपालीहरूको क्रिकेटप्रतिको उत्साहको प्रशंसा गरेका थिए।

३९ वर्षीय वार्नर आइतबार काठमाडौं आइपुगेका थिए। उनी एनपीएलमा काठमाडौं गोर्खाजबाट खेल्दैछन्। अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय क्रिकेटका तीनै प्रारूपमा १८ हजार ९९५ रन बनाएका वार्नरको सगरमाथा भ्रमणले नेपालको पर्यटन र प्राकृतिक सुन्दरताबारे अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय स्तरमा थप चर्चा हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

अग्निवीर योजनामा भारतको ठूलो परिवर्तन, २०२२ देखि रोकिएको गोर्खा भर्ती फेरि सुरु होला ?

भारत सरकारले अग्निपथ योजनाअन्तर्गत सैनिक सेवाको अवधि दुई वर्ष थप्ने निर्णय गरेसँगै सन् २०२२ देखि रोकिएको नेपाली गोर्खा भर्ती पुनः सुरु हुने सम्भावनाबारे चर्चा चुलिएको छ।

भारतीय प्रधानमन्त्री नरेन्द्र मोदीको अध्यक्षतामा बुधबार बसेको केन्द्रीय मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले अग्निवीर योजनाअन्तर्गत चार वर्ष सेवा पूरा गरेका सैनिकलाई थप दुई वर्ष सेवा गर्ने अवसर दिने निर्णय गरेको हो।

भारतले यस्तो निर्णय गरेको समयमा भारतीय विदेश सचिव विक्रम मिश्री दुईदिने नेपाल भ्रमणमा छन्। त्यस्तै, प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन शाहको भारत भ्रमणको तयारी पनि भइरहेको छ।

भारतीय पत्रिका द हिन्दू की कूटनीतिक मामिला सम्पादक सुहासिनी हैदरले पनि यो निर्णयको समयलाई नेपाल–भारत सम्बन्धका दृष्टिले महत्त्वपूर्ण मानेकी छन्। उनले सन् २०२२ देखि रोकिएको नेपाली गोर्खा भर्ती पुनः सुरु गर्न दुवै देश सहमत हुन सक्ने सम्भावनाबारे प्रश्न उठाएकी छन्।

यद्यपि, भारतको पछिल्लो निर्णयले नेपाली गोर्खा भर्ती खुल्ने औपचारिक घोषणा गरेको छैन। भर्ती पुनः सुरु हुने विषयमा नेपाल र भारतबीच सहमति हुन्छ वा हुँदैन भन्ने अझै स्पष्ट भइसकेको छैन।

Democrats Take Control of Congress, Putting Trump Under Pressure as Iran War, Ukraine Aid and Immigration Policies Face New Challenges

KATHMANDU — Democrats have won control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress, delivering a major political setback to President Donald Trump and creating new challenges for his administration. The Democratic Party's victory in the November 3 midterm elections means Republicans have lost their majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives. The result will make it harder for Trump to pass new laws and carry out his political agenda during the final two years of his presidency.

The election results reflect growing frustration among American voters over rising living costs, trade policies, immigration restrictions and the war with Iran. Democrats gained several seats in traditionally Republican states and districts, showing that many voters wanted stronger checks on Trump's administration. The victory also gives Democrats greater power to investigate the government, question officials and challenge presidential decisions.

What Does the Democratic Victory Mean for Trump?

The U.S. president has broad powers over foreign policy, national security, trade and immigration. However, Congress plays an important role in checking presidential authority. It approves government spending, passes national laws, investigates government activities and reviews many senior appointments.

With Democrats controlling both chambers, Trump will face stronger opposition when trying to pass new laws or secure funding for his policies. Democratic lawmakers will also lead important congressional committees, giving them greater power to investigate decisions made by the Trump administration.

However, the election result does not mean Trump has lost his presidential powers. He can still issue executive orders and make many decisions on trade, immigration and foreign policy without getting approval from Congress. Democrats can hold hearings, question government officials and challenge his decisions, but they cannot automatically cancel every policy introduced by the president.

The new Congress is expected to begin its work in January 2027. Until then, Republicans will continue to control both chambers, meaning the immediate balance of power in Washington will not change overnight.

Can Democrats Stop Trump's Trade Policies?

Trump's trade policies, especially his decision to impose high tariffs on goods from other countries, have been a major source of disagreement between Republicans and Democrats.

Trump has introduced heavy import taxes on products from both rival nations and long-standing U.S. allies, including Canada. He has argued that tariffs protect American industries and help strengthen the country's economy. However, critics say these policies increase costs for businesses and consumers.

Democrats have repeatedly criticized the tariffs but have struggled to challenge them because Republicans controlled Congress. Their new majority will give them more opportunities to question the administration's trade decisions and examine the economic impact of the tariffs.

However, Trump still has significant authority to impose tariffs through existing trade laws. According to James Smith, a market economist at Dutch bank ING, trade is one area where a president can take action without always needing congressional approval.

Democrats may use public hearings, investigations and other political tools to put pressure on the administration. But ending Trump's existing tariff policies will not be easy.

What Happens to Trump's Immigration Policies?

Immigration is another major issue that could create serious disagreements between Trump and the new Democratic Congress.

Trump has repeatedly defended his strict immigration policies, saying stronger border security is necessary to protect the United States and its citizens. His administration has introduced tougher measures targeting illegal immigration and border crossings.

Democrats have strongly criticized several of these policies, arguing that immigration enforcement should protect human rights and provide fair treatment to migrants.

With control of both chambers, Democrats will have more power to investigate immigration enforcement, question officials and challenge new government proposals. They could also use congressional hearings to examine how immigration laws are being implemented.

However, policies that are already in place will not automatically end because Democrats have won the election. Trump can continue using his executive powers, although new legislation and government funding decisions could become more difficult for his administration.

Can Congress Stop Trump From Going to War?

The war with Iran is expected to become one of the biggest sources of conflict between Trump and the new Democratic Congress.

Democratic lawmakers have repeatedly opposed the administration's military actions against Iran and have questioned whether Trump has sufficient legal authority to continue the conflict without congressional approval.

They have previously introduced three War Powers Resolution measures aimed at limiting Trump's military actions. One proposal passed the House of Representatives with support from some Republicans but failed to gain enough votes in the Senate.

Under the U.S. War Powers Resolution, the president must generally notify Congress within 48 hours of introducing U.S. forces into hostilities. Military action is generally limited to 60 days without congressional authorization, with a possible additional 30-day period for withdrawing forces.

Trump has argued that the military operation against Iran does not amount to a formal war. His administration has used this position to defend its actions without seeking a formal declaration of war from Congress.

Democrats could now increase pressure through investigations, hearings and legislation aimed at limiting military operations. They may also demand greater transparency about the cost, goals and legal basis of the conflict.

However, controlling Congress does not automatically give Democrats the power to stop every military action. The president remains commander in chief, and any major effort to restrict his authority could lead to a serious legal and political battle.

Could U.S. Policy Toward Iran Change?

The election result could also influence Trump's next decisions on Iran.

During the campaign, Trump suggested that the United States could take stronger military action against Iran after the election. However, he has also indicated that negotiations could offer a way to end the conflict.

Democrats have generally opposed expanding the war and have called for greater congressional oversight of military decisions.

Following the election results, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed that American voters had rejected the war against Iran. He said the Iranian government supported the American public's opposition to the conflict and warned that ignoring public opinion could have serious consequences for the United States.

Trump has not announced a major change in his Iran policy following the election. However, the new Democratic majority could make it politically more difficult for his administration to continue military operations without facing strong opposition in Congress.

Will America Resume Military Aid to Ukraine?

U.S. support for Ukraine could also become an important issue under the new congressional majority.

Trump recently halted some American assistance to Ukraine, saying he wants to end the war through negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. His administration has supported efforts to bring the two countries to the negotiating table, including talks expected to take place in Abu Dhabi.

Democrats, however, have generally supported continued military and financial assistance to Ukraine as it defends itself against Russia's invasion.

They have also criticized Trump's approach to negotiations, arguing that Ukraine should not be pressured into accepting an unfair agreement that benefits Russia.

With Democrats controlling both chambers, there could be renewed efforts to approve financial and military assistance for Kyiv. Democratic lawmakers may also use congressional oversight to question the administration's decisions on Ukraine.

The change in Congress could therefore offer Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy greater support in Washington. However, any major change in U.S. policy will depend on negotiations between Congress and the White House, as well as the availability of funding.

Can Democrats Remove Trump From Power?

Although Democrats have won control of Congress, the election does not automatically threaten Trump's position as president.

The president cannot be removed simply because his party loses its majority in the midterm elections. Congress can investigate the administration and begin impeachment proceedings if there are sufficient legal and political grounds. Removing a president through impeachment requires a two-thirds majority in the Senate to convict and remove him from office.

Democrats will not have enough votes to achieve that on their own.

They also cannot easily override a presidential veto. If Trump rejects a bill passed by Congress, lawmakers need a two-thirds majority in both the House and Senate to override his decision.

This means Trump will retain important powers even after Democrats take control of Congress. However, his ability to pass new laws and secure support for his policies will face much stronger resistance.

Trump Promises to Work With Democrats

Following the election results, Trump said he was willing to accept the outcome and work with Democrats. He congratulated the opposition party on its victory but rejected the idea that the result was a personal defeat.

Trump also indicated that he could use his presidential veto to block legislation he disagrees with. His comments suggest that cooperation between the White House and Congress may be difficult, especially on major issues such as immigration, trade and foreign policy.

Former President Barack Obama also responded to the election results on social media, saying the outcome could change the country's political direction. He criticized Trump's policies and said American voters wanted political leadership that brought people together rather than divided society.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan’s U.S. Senate race, making history as the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate. The 42-year-old progressive politician is a former public health official and a strong supporter of universal health care. However, his election victory does not mean he takes office immediately. He will join the Senate when his term officially begins.

Born and raised in southeastern Michigan, El-Sayed is the son of an Egyptian immigrant father. He studied at the University of Michigan, Oxford University, and Columbia University, where he earned degrees in public health and medicine. He previously served as director of the Detroit Health Department and later led the Wayne County Department of Health, Human Services, and Veterans Affairs. His political priorities include affordable health care, reducing living costs, and limiting the influence of wealthy donors in politics.

El-Sayed has clearly supported Ukraine in its war against Russia. Shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, he described the attack as an act of aggression against a democratic country. He praised countries that supported Ukraine by providing weapons and helping refugees. In an August 2026 interview with NBC's Meet the Press, he explained that Ukraine has the right to defend itself against an invasion by another country. He said supporting Ukraine is important for protecting international law and national independence.

His position on Israel is very different. El-Sayed has called for an immediate end to all U.S. military aid to Israel, including both offensive and defensive weapons. He has also supported restoring humanitarian funding for Palestinians, including support for UNRWA, the United Nations agency that helps Palestinian refugees. He has accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza. His position has created strong disagreements among voters, particularly within Michigan's Jewish community.

However, El-Sayed has said that both Palestinians and Israelis have the right to live in peace, dignity, and security. In a November 1, 2026, interview with 60 Minutes, he said Palestine has a right to exist. He also said Israel has a right to exist, while adding that both sides must agree on a fair political arrangement. He supports either a two-state solution or a single shared state if both communities freely choose that arrangement.

El-Sayed has also faced criticism over his comments about Hamas and an attack on a synagogue in Michigan. In October 2025, his campaign sent a fundraising email criticizing Israel's military actions in Gaza without mentioning Hamas's October 7, 2023, attack on Israel. The email drew criticism, although his campaign said it had been sent by mistake. A separate statement released by El-Sayed on the same day condemned Hamas's attack, the killings, and the taking of hostages.

In March 2026, after an attack on Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield, Michigan, El-Sayed condemned the violence and expressed support for the Jewish community. However, his later comments connecting the attack to the wider Middle East conflict angered some members of the community. In August, he apologized for those remarks, saying his initial condemnation should have been enough. He also stated that antisemitism must be opposed in all its forms.

El-Sayed's election has brought renewed attention to his foreign policy views, especially his different positions on Ukraine and Israel. He argues that supporting Ukraine is necessary because Russia invaded a sovereign country, while he opposes U.S. military support for Israel because of its actions in Gaza. However, his campaign statements do not guarantee how he will vote on every foreign aid proposal. His actual decisions on military assistance, funding, and foreign policy will become clearer after he officially takes his seat in the U.S. Senate.

नेपाली कांग्रेसले पार्टी र नेतृत्वविरुद्ध भइरहेको भनिएको षड्यन्त्र, दुष्प्रचार तथा राज्य संयन्त्रको दुरुपयोगविरुद्ध राजनीतिक र कानुनी रूपमा प्रतिवाद गर्ने जनाएको छ। महामन्त्री प्रदीप पौडेलले मंगलबार सार्वजनिक गरेको ६ बुँदे धारणामार्फत पार्टीको वैधानिकतामाथि उठाइएका प्रश्न र विभिन्न प्रचार निराधार तथा नियोजित भएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

कांग्रेसले २०८२ पुसमा सम्पन्न विशेष महाधिवेशन निर्वाचन आयोगबाट अद्यावधिक भइसकेको र सर्वोच्च अदालतबाट समेत वैधानिक ठहर भएको उल्लेख गरेको छ। साथै, २०८३ असोज १६ देखि २३ गतेसम्म १५औँ महाधिवेशन सम्पन्न भइसकेकाले पार्टीको वैधानिकतामाथि प्रश्न उठाउने प्रयास स्वीकार्य नहुने जनाएको छ।

वरिष्ठ उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले बुधबार पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्दै पार्टी र नेतृत्वविरुद्ध उठेका प्रश्न तथा छानबिनको सामना गर्न तयार रहेको बताए। उनले इनम सापकोटा प्रकरणमा प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयसँग सम्बन्धित व्यक्तिहरूको संलग्नतामा अनुसन्धानमा रहेका व्यक्ति र प्रमाणमाथि अनधिकृत नियन्त्रण तथा छेडछाड भएको भनिएका विषयको निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धान हुनुपर्ने माग गरे।

कांग्रेसले प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक हटाउने घटनालाई पनि यही घटनाक्रमसँग जोड्दै राज्य संयन्त्रको दुरुपयोग भएको आरोप लगाएको छ। पत्रकारमाथिको धरपकड, प्रेस नियन्त्रण र संवैधानिक निकायमाथिको हस्तक्षेपप्रति आपत्ति जनाउँदै पार्टीले कानुनी परामर्श र संसदीय पहल अघि बढाउने जनाएको छ।

कांग्रेसले सरकारलाई प्रतिपक्षलाई कमजोर बनाउने गतिविधि बन्द गरी विपद् प्रभावितको राहत, अर्थतन्त्रको पुनरुत्थान र जनसरोकारका विषयमा ध्यान दिन आग्रह गरेको छ।

प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) डा. मनोज केसीले दर्ज्यानी चिह्न लगाएका छन्। बुधबार गृह मन्त्रालयमा गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले उनलाई दर्ज्यानी चिह्न लगाइदिएका हुन्।

केसी बुधबार नै नेपाल प्रहरीको ३४औँ महानिरीक्षकमा नियुक्त भएका थिए। यसअघि आईजीपीलाई गृहसचिवले दर्ज्यानी चिह्न लगाइदिने परम्परा रहे पनि यसपटक गृहमन्त्री आफैँले चिह्न प्रदान गरेका छन्।

The Nepal Tourism Board has announced its first-ever Kukur Tihar Reel Competition 2026, offering a cash prize of Rs. 1 lakh to the winning creator. The competition aims to promote Nepal’s unique Kukur Tihar festival internationally through creative short videos highlighting the cultural significance of the festival and the special bond between humans and dogs.

To participate, creators must publish an original reel publicly on Instagram or Facebook using the hashtags #NepalFestival and #KukurTihar, while tagging the Nepal Tourism Board on the respective platform. The video must be in English or include English subtitles or an English voice-over.

Participants must also email their video to the Tourism Board with an accessible Google Drive link. The submission deadline is November 21, 2026. According to the Board, submitted reels may also be used for tourism promotion and digital communication.

The competition offers content creators an opportunity to showcase Nepal’s cultural traditions to an international audience while competing for a cash prize of Rs. 100,000.

A Saudi-based company has agreed to pay 181,000 Saudi riyals to the family of Bharat Mahato, a 45-year-old Nepali worker from Mahottari who was killed in a drone attack in Saudi Arabia. The amount includes 31,000 riyals in end-of-service benefits and 150,000 riyals in compensation.

The agreement was reached following an initiative by the Nepali Embassy in Riyadh. According to Nepali Labour Counsellor Kabiraj Upreti, the money will be sent to Bharat’s family after the necessary administrative procedures are completed. The company agreed to provide the compensation on humanitarian grounds after learning that Bharat’s labour permit had expired, potentially making his family ineligible for financial assistance from Nepal’s Foreign Employment Board and insurance.

Bharat had worked for the company for 14 years and was employed at an oil project operated by Saudi Aramco. He was killed on Kartik 4 in a drone attack targeting the Shaybah oil field in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province. The attack, attributed to Yemen’s Houthi rebels, also killed a Filipino worker.

Bharat was the main financial support for his family and had been building a house near his hometown. His wife is now facing the responsibility of raising their four children while dealing with an outstanding bank loan. Although the Nepali Embassy has completed the necessary procedures to bring his body home, flight disruptions have delayed its return, and the arrival date remains uncertain.

सरकारका प्रवक्ता एवं शिक्षामन्त्री सस्मित पोखरेलले नेपाल प्रहरीका प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) दानबहादुर कार्कीको जिम्मेवारी हेरफेर पार्टीको निर्देशनपछि गरिएको बताएका छन्।

बुधबार बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकपछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै मन्त्री पोखरेलले बदलिँदो परिस्थितिका कारण पार्टीबाट सरकारलाई संवेदनशील विषयमा आवश्यक कदम चाल्न निर्देशन आएको बताएका हुन्।

‘धेरै ठाउँबाट अहिले बदलिँदो परिस्थिति छ । पार्टीबाट पनि संवेदनशील विषयमा सरकारले केही गर्नुपर्‍यो भनेर निर्देशन आएको थियो,’ मन्त्री पोखरेलले भने, ‘त्यसपछि जिम्मेवारी हेरफेर गरिएको हो।’

उनले प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई शान्ति सुरक्षासम्बन्धी सल्लाह दिने जिम्मेवारी पनि निकै संवेदनशील हुने उल्लेख गरे। यस्तो जिम्मेवारीको महत्वलाई ध्यानमा राखेर निर्णय गरिएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

सरकारको यो अभिव्यक्तिले नेपाल प्रहरीको नेतृत्व परिवर्तनमा पार्टीको निर्देशनले भूमिका खेलेको विषयलाई थप चर्चामा ल्याएको छ।

ईजीपीबाट हटाइए दानबहादुर कार्की, मनोज केसीलाई दिइयो जिम्मेवारी!

नेपाल प्रहरीको नेतृत्व परिवर्तनलाई लिएर राजनीतिक तथा सुरक्षा वृत्तमा चर्चा चर्किएको छ। प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई पदबाट हटाएर अतिरिक्त प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (एआईजी) डा. मनोजकुमार केसीलाई जिम्मेवारी दिइएको दाबी सार्वजनिक भए पनि यसको आधिकारिक पुष्टि हुन सकेको छैन।

पछिल्ला दिनमा सरकार र प्रहरी नेतृत्वबीच मतभेद देखिएको भन्ने समाचार सार्वजनिक भएपछि आईजीपी परिवर्तनको चर्चा सुरु भएको थियो। कार्कीलाई हटाउने तयारी भइरहेको विवरण आएपछि प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयमा उच्च अधिकारीहरूको आकस्मिक बैठकसमेत बसेको थियो।

अक्टोबर २९ मा काठमाडौंको नक्सालस्थित प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयमा बसेको बैठक करिब पाँच घण्टा चलेको थियो। उक्त बैठकमा प्रहरी संगठनको व्यावसायिकता, नेतृत्वमाथि भइरहेको चर्चा र संगठनभित्रको अवस्थाबारे छलफल भएको समाचार प्रकाशित भएको थियो।

राजीनामाको समाचार प्रहरीद्वारा खण्डन

आईजीपी कार्कीले आफूलाई सरकारले राजीनामा दिन भनेको भन्ने विवरण असत्य रहेको बताएका थिए। नेपाल प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयले पनि उनको राजीनामासम्बन्धी समाचार भ्रामक भएको भन्दै खण्डन गरेको थियो।

यसैबीच, एआईजी डा. मनोजकुमार केसीको नाम नयाँ प्रहरी प्रमुखका सम्भावित उम्मेदवारका रूपमा चर्चामा आएको छ। केसी नेपाल प्रहरीका अनुभवी अधिकारी हुन्। उनले केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरोलगायत विभिन्न महत्त्वपूर्ण जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका छन्।

नक्कली भुटानी शरणार्थी प्रकरणको अनुसन्धानमा भूमिका निर्वाह गरेका कारण केसी सार्वजनिक चर्चामा आएका प्रहरी अधिकारीमध्ये एक हुन्।

प्रहरी नेतृत्व परिवर्तनमा सरकारको निर्णय महत्त्वपूर्ण

प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकको नियुक्ति तथा पदबाट हटाउने विषय कानुनी प्रक्रियासँग सम्बन्धित हुन्छ। यसका लागि सरकारको औपचारिक निर्णय आवश्यक पर्छ।

हाल नेपाल प्रहरीको आधिकारिक वेबसाइटमा दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई नै प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकका रूपमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ। मनोजकुमार केसीलाई नयाँ आईजीपी नियुक्त गरिएको पुष्टि हुने सरकारी निर्णय उपलब्ध भएको छैन।

प्रहरी नेतृत्व परिवर्तनको चर्चा चर्किए पनि औपचारिक निर्णय नभएसम्म कार्की पदबाट हटेको वा केसीले नयाँ जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेको भन्न मिल्दैन।

यसरी नेपाल प्रहरीको नेतृत्व परिवर्तनबारे व्यापक चर्चा भइरहेका बेला अब सरकारको आधिकारिक निर्णयले मात्रै नयाँ प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक को हुने भन्ने विषय स्पष्ट पार्नेछ।

बागलुङमा राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का स्थानीय नेता अमर खड्काको घरमा जुवा खेलिरहेको अवस्थामा प्रहरीले ९ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको छ।

गोप्य सूचनाका आधारमा प्रहरीले छापा मार्दा खड्कासहित ९ जना तास खेलिरहेको अवस्थामा भेटिएको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ। उनीहरूको साथबाट १ लाख ६४ हजार ९२५ रुपैयाँ नगद बरामद भएको छ।

पक्राउ पर्नेमा बागलुङ नगरपालिका–२ का चिरञ्जीवी शर्मा, रिपोर्ट जिसी, दुर्गाबहादुर खत्री, हरि शर्मा र भीमबहादुर खत्री छन्। त्यस्तै डम्मरबहादुर भण्डारी, राजु गौतम र केशव पराजुली पनि पक्राउ परेका छन्।

प्रहरीका अनुसार पक्राउ परेकाहरूमा नेता, वकिल र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीसमेत रहेका छन्। उनीहरूमाथि थप अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ।

खड्का यसअघि नेपाली कांग्रेसमा आबद्ध थिए। प्रतिनिधिसभा निर्वाचनअघि उनी रास्वपा प्रवेश गरेका थिए। उनी बागलुङ नगरपालिकाका पार्टी वडासभापति हुन्।

समाचार कक्षभित्रै प्रवेश गरेर पत्रकारमाथि गरिएको प्रहरी धरपकडबारे सरकारले आफूलाई पूर्वजानकारी नभएको स्पष्टीकरण दिएको छ। सरकारका प्रवक्ता सस्मित पोखरेलले उक्त कार्य प्रहरीको आन्तरिक अनुसन्धानका लागि भएको र सरकार वा प्रधानमन्त्रीबाट अनुमति नलिइएको बताएका छन्।

१७ कात्तिकमा सिंहदरबारमा मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकपछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै पोखरेलले प्रहरीको आन्तरिक सूचना चुहावटबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न पत्रकारसँग सोधपुछ गरिएको दाबी गरे। प्रधानमन्त्रीले आईजीपीको राजीनामा मागेको वा कारबाही गर्न लागेको भन्ने भ्रामक सूचना कहाँबाट आयो भन्ने विषयमा प्रहरीले तथ्य बुझ्न खोजेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

पोखरेलका अनुसार समाचार प्रकाशित हुने प्रक्रियाबारे बुझ्न प्रहरीले आफ्नै तवरबाट सोधपुछ गरेको हो। यसमा सरकारसँग पूर्ण अनुमति लिइएको थिएन र प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन शाहलाई पनि यसबारे पूर्वजानकारी थिएन।

उनले घटनाबारे जानकारी पाएपछि प्रधानमन्त्रीले कुनै पनि पत्रकारलाई सोधपुछका नाममा हिरासतमा नराख्न निर्देशन दिएको बताए। साथै, पत्रकारलाई गिरफ्तार वा नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको नभई सोधपुछ मात्रै गरिएको सरकारको दाबी छ।

बिचौलिया इनम सापकोटासँगको सम्बन्धका कारण विवादमा परेका सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीश हरिप्रसाद फुयालमाथि अन्य न्यायाधीशहरूले फुलकोर्ट बैठकमै आक्रोश व्यक्त गरेका छन्। सिंगो न्यायालयलाई विवादमा तानेको भन्दै उनीहरूले फुयाललाई ‘तपाईं मात्र विचलित हुनुभएन, हामी सबैलाई डुबाउनुभयो’ भनेको स्रोतको भनाइ छ।

शुक्रबार र आइतबार बसेको पूर्ण बैठकमा न्यायाधीशहरूले होटेल हिमालयमा सापकोटासँग भेट्न गएका अन्य न्यायाधीशहरूको नाम सार्वजनिक गर्न फुयालसँग माग गरेका थिए। केही व्यक्तिको गलत आचरणको भार सिंगो न्यायालयले बोक्न नसक्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ थियो। फुयालले भने आफूले केही गल्ती स्वीकार गर्दै आन्तरिक छानबिन गर्न प्रस्ताव गरेको बताइएको छ।

फुयालले आफ्नो विषय संसदीय छानबिनमा गए धेरै कुरा बाहिर आउन सक्ने र सबैलाई अप्ठ्यारो पर्न सक्ने भन्दै आन्तरिक छानबिनलाई उचित विकल्पका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेका थिए। उनले छानबिन भए होटेल हिमालयमा गएका अन्य व्यक्तिको नामसमेत खुलाउन सक्ने बताएका थिए। तर, सर्वोच्चको पूर्ण बैठकले आन्तरिक छानबिन समिति गठन नगरी संसदीय छानबिनमार्फत सत्यतथ्य बाहिर ल्याउनुपर्ने संकेत गरेको छ।

बैठकमा सापकोटासँगको सम्पर्कबारे प्रधानन्यायाधीश मनोजकुमार शर्मालाई जानकारी नगराएको विषयमा पनि फुयालसँग प्रश्न गरिएको थियो। साथै, आफूले चिनेको र आफूसँग सम्बन्ध जोडिएको व्यक्तिको बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरण मुद्दा आफैँले हेरेको तथा त्यसको फैसलाबारे सार्वजनिक रूपमा बोलेको विषयमा समेत उनको आलोचना भएको थियो।

सापकोटासँगको ह्वाट्सएप कुराकानी सार्वजनिक भएपछि फुयालले उनीसँग भेटेको स्वीकार गरेका थिए। महाअभियोगको त्रासका कारण भेटेको र कुनै गलत नियत नरहेको उनको दाबी छ। यसैबीच, नेपाल बार एसोसिएसनले घटनाको अध्ययन गर्न पूर्वअध्यक्ष चण्डेश्वर श्रेष्ठको नेतृत्वमा ६ सदस्यीय समिति गठन गरेको छ। फुयालले कात्तिक २० गतेसम्म बिदा लिएका छन्।

सत्तारूढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीले यस प्रकरणमा संसदीय छानबिन गर्ने निर्णय गरिसकेको छ भने सर्वोच्चको पूर्ण बैठकले पनि संसदीय छानबिनबाट सत्यतथ्य बाहिर ल्याउन आग्रह गरेको छ।

राष्ट्रिय प्रजातन्त्र पार्टी (राप्रपा) की प्रमुख सचेतक खुश्बु ओलीले एकदुई जना न्यायाधीशमाथि महाभियोग लगाउँदैमा न्यायालयमा देखिएका विकृति र विसंगति अन्त्य नहुने बताएकी छन्। उनले न्यायालय सुधारका लागि समग्र पुनःसंरचना आवश्यक रहेको भन्दै सरकारलाई यस विषयमा गम्भीर बन्न आग्रह गरेकी छन्।

सोमबार नेपाली कांग्रेसको आह्वानमा सिंहदरबारमा बसेको प्रतिपक्षी दलहरूको बैठकपछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै ओलीले न्यायालयको विषयलाई संसद्मा गम्भीर बहसको विषय बनाउनुपर्ने बताइन्।

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशदेखि प्रधानन्यायाधीशसम्मको नाम जोडेर विभिन्न घटना सार्वजनिक भइरहँदा न्यायालयप्रति सर्वसाधारणको विश्वास कमजोर हुँदै गएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

‘एकदुई जना व्यक्तिमाथि महाभियोग लगाउँदैमा न्यायालयको समग्र सुधार सम्भव हुँदैन,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘न्यायालयको पुनःसंरचनामा सरकार गम्भीर हुनुपर्छ। न्यायालयको विषयलाई संसद्मा गम्भीर बहसमा लैजान यथाशीघ्र संसद् आह्वान गर्नुपर्छ।’

ओलीले न्यायालयमा देखिएका समस्या समाधानका लागि सीमित व्यक्तिमाथिको कारबाहीभन्दा पनि संस्थागत सुधारमा ध्यान दिनुपर्ने धारणा राखिन्।

उनले न्यायालयको विषयसँगै प्रहरी र सरकारबीचको सम्बन्ध तथा अर्थमन्त्री स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले भारतमा दिएको अभिव्यक्तिबारे पनि संसद्मा छलफल हुनुपर्ने बताइन्।

प्रतिपक्षी दलहरूको बैठकले सरकारसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न विषय संसद्मा उठाउनुपर्ने धारणा राखिरहेका बेला राप्रपाले पनि तत्काल संसद् अधिवेशन आह्वान गर्न माग गरेको हो।

माधव नेपाल र मिनेन्द्र रिजालसहित ९४ जनाविरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दा, ७६ करोड बिगो दाबी!

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री माधवकुमार नेपाल र नेपाली कांग्रेसका नेता तथा पूर्वमन्त्री डा. मिनेन्द्र रिजालसहितका व्यक्तिविरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दा दायर गरेको छ। सरकारी जग्गा गैरकानुनी रूपमा छुट दर्ता, सट्टापट्टा तथा बिक्री गरिएको आरोपमा अख्तियारले विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा अघि बढाएको हो।

मोरङको विराटनगर र सुनसरीको इटहरी क्षेत्रसँग जोडिएको रिजाल क्यानिङ कम्पनी तथा रिजाल टासी इन्डस्ट्रिजको जग्गा प्रकरणमा अनियमितता भएको अख्तियारको दाबी छ।

अख्तियारका अनुसार कम्पनीको नाममा रहेको हदबन्दीभन्दा बढी जग्गा मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयमार्फत सट्टापट्टा गर्न अनुमति दिइएको थियो। त्यसपछि मूल्यवान् जग्गा बिक्री गरी अन्य स्थानको जग्गासँग सट्टापट्टा गरिएको विषयमा अनुसन्धान गरिएको हो।

तत्कालीन प्रधानमन्त्री माधवकुमार नेपाल नेतृत्वको मन्त्रिपरिषद्ले गरेको निर्णय र त्यसमा तत्कालीन मन्त्री मिनेन्द्र रिजालको भूमिकालाई समेत अनुसन्धानको दायरामा ल्याइएको छ।

मन्त्रिपरिषद्को निर्णयमाथि प्रश्न

यो प्रकरणमा मन्त्रिपरिषद्बाट भएको निर्णयका आधारमा सार्वजनिक जग्गा व्यक्तिको स्वामित्वमा गएको वा कम्पनीलाई गैरकानुनी लाभ पुगेको भन्ने विषयमा अख्तियारले प्रश्न उठाएको छ।

आरोपपत्रमा तत्कालीन सरकारी अधिकारी, भूमि प्रशासनसँग सम्बन्धित कर्मचारी तथा जग्गा कारोबारमा संलग्न व्यक्तिहरूको भूमिकाबारे समेत अनुसन्धान गरिएको छ।

मुद्दामा पूर्वमन्त्री डम्बर श्रेष्ठ, पूर्वसचिव छविराज पन्त तथा भूमि व्यवस्थासँग सम्बन्धित अन्य उच्चपदस्थ अधिकारीहरू पनि प्रतिवादीको सूचीमा रहेको समाचार सार्वजनिक भएको छ।

९४ जना र ७६ करोडको प्रारम्भिक विवरण

मुद्दा दायर भएको सुरुवाती समाचारहरूमा माधव नेपाल र मिनेन्द्र रिजालसहित ९४ जनालाई प्रतिवादी बनाउँदै करिब ७६ करोड रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबी गरिएको उल्लेख थियो।

तर पछि सार्वजनिक भएका विवरणमा प्रतिवादीको संख्या र बिगो रकम फरक देखिएको छ। अनलाइनखबर र नागरिक न्यूजले ९७ जना प्रतिवादी तथा करिब ७३ करोड ४९ लाख रुपैयाँ बिगो दाबी गरिएको विवरण प्रकाशित गरेका छन्।

यस मुद्दामा केही व्यक्तिलाई जग्गा जफत गर्ने प्रयोजनका लागि मात्र विपक्षी बनाइएको समेत उल्लेख छ।

अदालतबाट हुन बाँकी छ अन्तिम फैसला

माधवकुमार नेपाल र मिनेन्द्र रिजालविरुद्ध भ्रष्टाचार मुद्दा दायर भए पनि उनीहरू दोषी प्रमाणित भइसकेका छैनन्। अख्तियारले लगाएका आरोप, प्रस्तुत प्रमाण र प्रतिवादीहरूको जवाफको परीक्षणपछि विशेष अदालतले निर्णय गर्नेछ।

बेलायत जाने नेपालीका लागि दुःखको खबर! पीआर पाउन १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने!

अध्ययन, रोजगारी तथा स्थायी बसोबासको सपना बोकेर बेलायत जाने तयारीमा रहेका नेपालीहरूका लागि महत्त्वपूर्ण खबर सार्वजनिक भएको छ। बेलायत सरकारले विदेशी नागरिकलाई स्थायी बसोबास अनुमति अर्थात् पीआर प्राप्त गर्न लाग्ने समय बढाउने नयाँ नीति अघि सारेको छ। यसअनुसार अधिकांश विदेशी कामदारले अब पाँच वर्षको सट्टा १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था प्रस्ताव गरिएको छ।

बेलायतकी गृहमन्त्री शबाना महमुदले नोभेम्बर २ मा संसद्मा नयाँ अध्यागमन नीतिबारे जानकारी दिएकी हुन्। सरकारले यसलाई ‘अर्न्ड सेटलमेन्ट’ (Earned Settlement) नाम दिएको छ। यो व्यवस्थाअनुसार बेलायतमा कति वर्ष बसेको छ भन्ने मात्रै नभई व्यक्तिको आम्दानी, रोजगारी, आचरण तथा देशप्रतिको योगदानलाई पनि स्थायी बसोबासको आधार बनाइनेछ।

यसअघि बेलायतमा निश्चित प्रकारका कामदार भिसामा गएका विदेशी नागरिकले सामान्यतया पाँच वर्षपछि स्थायी बसोबासका लागि आवेदन दिन पाउने व्यवस्था थियो। तर नयाँ योजनाले अधिकांश कामदारका लागि उक्त अवधि दोब्बर बनाउनेछ।

सबैले १० वर्ष कुर्नुपर्ने भने होइन

बेलायत सरकारले सबै विदेशी नागरिकका लागि एउटै नियम लागू गर्ने भनेको छैन। वार्षिक ५० हजार पाउन्डभन्दा बढी आम्दानी भएका योग्य कामदार तथा डाक्टर, नर्स र शिक्षकजस्ता सार्वजनिक सेवाका केही कर्मचारीले पाँच वर्षमै स्थायी बसोबासका लागि आवेदन दिन सक्नेछन्।

त्यस्तै, वार्षिक एक लाख २५ हजार पाउन्डभन्दा बढी कमाउने उच्च आय भएका व्यक्तिले निश्चित सर्त पूरा गरे तीन वर्षमै स्थायी बसोबासको अवसर पाउन सक्नेछन्।

किसानले उत्पादन गरेको दूधको भुक्तानी कर्मचारीका व्यक्तिगत खातामा जम्मा गरेर दुग्ध विकास संस्थान (डिडिसी) मा १२ करोड रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी घोटाला गरेको खुलेको छ । नेपाल प्रहरीको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरो (सिआइबी) ले गरेको अनुसन्धानमा तत्कालीन महाप्रबन्धक सञ्जीव झासहित कर्मचारीहरूको मिलेमतोमा रकम हिनामिना भएको देखिएको हो ।

गत जेठ ७ गते परेको उजुरीका आधारमा अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको सिआइबीले लैनचौरस्थित डिडिसीको केन्द्रीय कार्यालय र बालाजुस्थित काठमाडौं दुग्ध कार्यालयमा छापा मारेर कागजात नियन्त्रणमा लिएको थियो । अनुसन्धानका क्रममा १७ वटा कृषि तथा पशुपालन फार्म र सहकारीमार्फत कर्मचारीका खातामा रकम गएको खुलेको छ ।

कर्मचारीहरूले किसानलाई दूधमा रहेको चिल्लो पदार्थ र एसएनएफको वास्तविक विवरण नदिई बढी भुक्तानी देखाउने र त्यसको केही रकम आफ्नो खातामा फिर्ता लिन लगाउने गरेको अनुसन्धानमा खुलेको छ । कतिपय अवस्थामा किसानले पठाएको दूधमा समस्या आएको भन्दै अर्को फार्मको दूध थपेर परिमाण बढाउने र थप देखाइएको रकम कर्मचारीले लिने गरेको पाइएको छ ।

अनुसन्धानअनुसार लालीगुराँस पशुपालन फार्मबाट मात्रै कर्मचारीको खातामा चार करोड ४२ लाख रुपैयाँ आएको छ । दुर्घटनामा मृत्यु भएका रितेश राय यादवको खातामा विभिन्न कृषि फार्मबाट दुई करोड ७८ लाख रुपैयाँ जम्मा भएको देखिएको छ । त्यस्तै रामकेवल रायको खातामा एक करोड १४ लाख र उनका छोरा जितेन्द्रकुमार यादवको खातामा एक करोड ३२ लाख रुपैयाँ आएको सिआइबीको अनुसन्धानमा उल्लेख छ ।

यसैगरी, कर्मचारी मनहरि शर्माको खातामा एक करोड १५ लाख, शिवनन्द रायको खातामा एक करोड ६९ लाख र नवीन राय यादवले एक करोड ९३ लाख रुपैयाँ लिएको अनुसन्धानबाट खुलेको छ । तत्कालीन महाप्रबन्धक झाको कार्यकालमा मात्रै पाँच करोड रुपैयाँ घोटाला भएको सिआइबीको दाबी छ ।

यस प्रकरणमा तत्कालीन महाप्रबन्धक झासहित आठ जना पक्राउ परिसकेका छन् । केही अन्य व्यक्ति फरार रहेको र उनीहरूको खोजी भइरहेको सिआइबीले जनाएको छ । पक्राउ परेकाहरूमाथि आपराधिक विश्वासघात र संगठित अपराधसम्बन्धी कसुरमा अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ । अदालतले उनीहरूलाई सात दिन हिरासतमा राख्न अनुमति दिएको छ ।

सिआइबीका प्रमुख एआईजी उमाप्रसाद चतुर्वेदीले किसानको रकम नेतृत्वदेखि तल्लो तहका कर्मचारीसम्मको मिलेमतोमा हिनामिना भएको अनुसन्धानबाट खुलेको बताएका छन् ।

हालै सार्वजनिक भएको ‘हुरुन इन्डिया रिच लिस्ट २०२६’ अनुसार शाहरुख खान भारतका अन्य चर्चित अभिनेता अमिताभ बच्चन, सलमान खान र ऋतिक रोशनलाई पछि पार्दै सबैभन्दा धनी अभिनेता बनेका हुन्।

यसैगरी विभिन्न अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय ब्रान्डका विज्ञापन, व्यापारिक साझेदारी तथा घरजग्गामा गरिएको लगानीले पनि उनको आर्थिक साम्राज्य विस्तार भएको छ।

The real story: Two female belugas with marked spinal deformities washed ashore on the banks of the St. Lawrence River in Quebec and were examined at the Université de Montréal's Faculty of Veterinary Medicine with CT scans. Both were emaciated. In the first, a 17-year-old female, arthritis caused by the deformities likely contributed to her death. Source: Canadian Wildlife Health Cooperative (CWHC-Quebec), published 2026.

Researchers who watch St. Lawrence belugas from boats had seen it before: now and then, a living whale with a visibly bent spine. What nobody had done was examine one up close. Then two female belugas with marked spinal deformities washed ashore on the banks of the river, and the Quebec team of the Canadian Wildlife Health Cooperative finally had the chance.

Both whales were taken to the Université de Montréal's Faculty of Veterinary Medicine for post-mortem examination and computed tomography scans. Both were emaciated. In the first, a 17-year-old young adult female, the scientists found significant degenerative osteoarthritis secondary to the spinal deformities. They concluded that these bone malformations ultimately contributed to her death, most likely by making it harder for her to move and feed.

The finding is both small and large. A preliminary review of photographs of living belugas collected since 2003 by the Group for Research and Education on Marine Mammals suggests that vertebral deformities are present in fewer than 3 percent of the whales photographed. What causes them is still not known; the researchers say the two examinations "pave the way" for further investigation. For a population already struggling to raise calves, every animal that can't hunt properly is another loss, and a question still waiting for an answer.

Follow Blue Depths for more real ocean moments, captured as they happen.

The war in Ukraine has taken a devastating toll on wildlife in the Black Sea. Experts have reported that more than 120,000 dolphins have died since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

Military activity, underwater explosions, intense noise from naval vessels, and pollution have been identified as potential threats to marine life. Dolphins rely heavily on sound to navigate, communicate, and find food, making underwater disturbances especially dangerous.

The reported death toll highlights the often-overlooked environmental consequences of war, extending far beyond the battlefield and affecting marine ecosystems.

When the Chinese struck at Chosin Reservoir in late November 1950, Colonel Homer Litzenberg's 7th Marines were holding the exposed northern flank at Yudam-ni — the first to take the blow and the last to pull back. His regiment fought through some of the worst winter combat in American history, much of it at night, much of it hand to hand.

Litzenberg had drilled his men relentlessly, and it showed: the 7th Marines held together when units around them were coming apart. He later said the real heroes were the nineteen-year-old riflemen who stood their ground in cold that froze weapons solid.

For Chosin he received the Navy Cross. He never bragged about it. The regiment's stand said everything.

#HomerLitzenberg #ChosinReservoir #USMC #KoreanWar #NeverForget

In November 1950, Major General Oliver P. Smith's 1st Marine Division was strung out around the Chosin Reservoir in North Korea when some 120,000 Chinese troops closed in around them. It was fifty degrees below zero, the wounded were freezing in their sleeping bags, and every road out ran through the enemy.

Smith refused to panic. He built a rolling perimeter, brought up air support, and marched his division seventy miles through the Chinese lines to the sea at Hungnam — bringing out not just his men but the Army units trapped alongside them. Asked if this was a retreat, he gave the line that defined him: "Retreat, hell! We're just attacking in a different direction."

#OliverPSmith #ChosinReservoir #USMC #KoreanWar #NeverForget

A newly released minority report from Democrats on the Congressional Joint Economic Committee reveals that President Donald Trump's personal stock holdings in the oil and gas sector have surged in value to between $22.5 million and $81.6 million, up from an estimated $12.6 million to $46 million at the end of 2025. 

Based on Office of Government Ethics filings and market analytics, the committee's analysis found that the President’s energy portfolio has climbed by an average of roughly 43% in value since late 2025. The report also highlights active trading, noting between $4.7 million and $17.5 million in new oil and gas stock purchases alongside several million dollars in sales during the middle of the year. 

Capitol Hill Democrats and government ethics watchdogs argue that the massive portfolio growth creates an unprecedented conflict of interest, alleging that executive wartime decisions and geopolitical friction with Tehran have directly driven up domestic energy profits while raising costs for ordinary consumers at the gas pump. 

Allies and industry advocates maintain that broader market dynamics, resilient domestic production, and long-term energy independence initiatives naturally drive sector valuations, asserting that standard broad-market or blind portfolio management practices adhere to disclosure requirements.

BREAKING: The U.S. Navy has recorded a decade-high spike in catastrophic accidents, reporting 16 Class A aviation mishaps and 11 serious afloat incidents in fiscal year 2026—the highest total since 2014.

The military classifies an incident as a Class A mishap when it results in a fatality, permanent total disability, the complete destruction of an aircraft, or damage exceeding $2.5 million.

Over the past 12 months, carrier strike groups and naval aviation squadrons have faced unrelenting operational pressure—ranging from sustained combat engagements in the Red Sea to high-tempo deterrence patrols across the Indo-Pacific and Mediterranean.

The spike in major incidents has reignited fierce debate across the defense community regarding the root causes:

Relentless operational tempo and extended deployments wearing down crews

Severe maintenance backlogs, parts cannibalization, and shipyard delays

Retention shortfalls among experienced aviation mechanics and crew chiefs

Aging airframes pushed past their intended operational service life

When maintenance intervals are cut short and flight crews are stretched thin, the margin for error on a carrier flight deck shrinks to zero.

To our sailors, aviators, and maintainers: what is the biggest factor driving this spike in mishaps? Is it burnout, parts availability, or leadership pressure?

Brigadier General Anna Mae Hays led the Army Nurse Corps through the Vietnam War — and on June 11, 1970, she became the first woman in American history to wear a general's stars. No woman in any American armed service had ever held general rank before.

Hays had served in World War II, Korea, and Vietnam, building the nursing force that kept the Army's medical system running through three wars. She fought for her nurses' recognition, their working conditions, and their place in a military that wasn't built for them.

She didn't just break the glass ceiling. She did it in uniform, while running a war's worth of hospitals — and she held the door open for every woman who followed.

#AnnaMaeHays #ArmyNurse #VietnamWar #Trailblazer #NeverForget

Two Women Shatter Precedent By Pushing Deep Into Navy SEAL BUD/S Pipeline
Two female candidates attempting to earn the coveted Navy SEAL trident have advanced further through the military's grueling selection pipeline than any women in history. According to investigative reporting from CBS News, an enlisted sailor and a commissioned naval officer entered Basic Underwater Demolition/SEAL (BUD/S) training at Naval Amphibious Base Coronado in California, conquering the brutal initial conditioning weeks that eliminate nearly half of every class.

Key Historic Milestones
Historic Hell Week Milestone
The enlisted candidate broke all prior records by entering Hell Week, the punishing 5.5-day crucible that involves around 200 miles of running, freezing surf immersion, and barely four hours of total sleep, before being medically withdrawn.

Conquering The 45 Percent Drop Gate
Navy records compiled between 1998 and 2023 document that roughly 45 percent of all candidates voluntarily quit or get dropped during the three weeks preceding Hell Week, underscoring the exceptional endurance required to reach week four.

Naval Officer Performance
The female naval officer advanced into the third week of Phase 1 before being rolled back to a subsequent training class and subsequently requesting a voluntary drop prior to Hell Week.

Naval Special Warfare Precedent
While no woman has completed SEAL qualification since combat exclusions were lifted in 2016, Naval Special Warfare previously saw its first female graduate in 2021 when a sailor successfully completed the rigorous pipeline to become a Special Warfare Combatant-Craft Crewman (SWCC).

What does true brotherhood look like when surviving seems impossible, yet you choose to keep firing so your teammate has a chance to live?

Petty Officer Second Class Matthew Gene “Axe” Axelson was just 29 years old and married for two years when a reconnaissance mission in the rugged Hindu Kush mountains of Kunar Province, Afghanistan, took his life on June 28, 2005.

Inserted on a high-stakes mission during Operation Red Wings alongside Lt. Michael P. Murphy, Danny Dietz, and Marcus Luttrell, the four-man reconnaissance team was compromised and rapidly surrounded by a heavily armed insurgent force holding the high ground.

 Despite suffering multiple grievous gunshot wounds in the chaotic firefight, Axelson refused to fall back or yield. According to his official Navy Cross citation, he urged his closest teammate to escape while he continued engaging enemy fighters, providing covering fire until he was mortally wounded.

The brutal engagement ultimately claimed the lives of Axelson, Murphy, and Dietz, along with 16 special operators and aviators aboard the downed MH-47 rescue helicopter leaving Luttrell as the sole survivor of the initial team. Axelson was posthumously awarded the Navy Cross for his extraordinary heroism and selfless devotion to his brothers-in-arms.

Engineered at the legendary Skunk Works facility for NASA’s Quesst mission, the nearly 100-foot-long experimental aircraft is built to solve one of aviation’s oldest hurdles. Its radical layout features an elongated 30-foot needle nose and an engine mounted directly atop the fuselage, geometry shaped to disperse supersonic shockwaves before they can merge into a window-rattling sonic boom. Because the elongated nose completely blocks forward cockpit sightlines, test pilots fly without a forward windshield, relying instead on NASA’s eXternal Vision System to stream a real-time 4K camera feed of the airspace onto an interior display.

Cruising at Mach 1.4 at 55,000 feet, the aircraft softens the traditional sonic boom into a gentle acoustic thump on the ground. NASA plans to use flight-test acoustics from overland runs to provide data to regulators and potentially lift the decades-old ban on commercial overland supersonic flight.

Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky is preparing to force a historic House floor vote to impeach Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth when Congress reconvenes next week. Massie confirmed the maneuver during an interview with CNN, claiming multiple Republican lawmakers have privately signaled their willingness to vote in favor of removing the Pentagon chief.

The push marks a significant escalation in Capitol Hill friction over executive war-making authorities and military operations conducted without congressional authorization.

Privileged Floor Motion
Because Massie plans to introduce the measure as a privileged resolution, House leadership cannot easily bury it in committee, forcing lawmakers to take an on-the-record vote within legislative days.

Bipartisan Dissatisfaction
Massie stated that cross-party frustration has mounted over Pentagon leadership decisions, including prolonged combat operations abroad and defense personnel controversies outlined by The Guardian.

Constitutional War Powers Challenge
The underlying impeachment charges stem from allegations that military operations were sustained beyond statutory limits without formal approval from Capitol Hill, as highlighted in Rep. Massie's legislative statement.

In 1968, First Lieutenant Diane Carlson Evans arrived in Vietnam as an Army nurse, serving in evacuation hospitals where the wounded came in by helicopter around the clock. She did what thousands of American women did in that war: she saved lives, comforted the dying, and carried on.

But Evans saw that when the war ended, the women who served were being written out of its history. So she founded the Vietnam Women's Memorial Project and spent a decade fighting Washington bureaucracy until, in 1993, a bronze memorial to America's women veterans was dedicated on the National Mall.

Nurses don't always make the history books. Diane Carlson Evans made sure they finally did.

#DianeCarlsonEvans #ArmyNurse #VietnamWar #Nurses #NeverForget

The Marine Corps wants drones that can do one of the hardest, least glamorous jobs in the field: deliver supplies to small units with no runway, no truck, and no safe way to be reached.

In early 2027, the Marine Corps and Navy will invite companies to Huntsville, Alabama, to demonstrate cargo drones for a program called TRUAS. The requirements are demanding. One flight: carry 100 pounds up to 40 nautical miles in calm air, drop it, and return without refueling. Another: haul at least 150 pounds. All without catapults, nets, or cables, launching and landing on open ground.

The autonomy goals are the striking part. The drones must size up a landing zone on their own, day or night, spotting people, slopes, and hazards, and avoid other aircraft like a human pilot would.

It reflects a fast shift: as the ground grows too exposed to cross, logistics is moving into the air, onto machines that fly themselves.

Nancy Lacore, the Navy admiral Pete Hegseth fired and a 35-year Navy veteran, defeated her MAGA Republican opponent last night to win South Carolina’s 1st District House seat. After decades of service in uniform, she’s heading to Congress—and now Hegseth will have to answer to her there.

On June 17, 1966, Navy pilot Paul Galanti was shot down over North Vietnam. He spent nearly seven years in the "Hanoi Hilton," enduring torture and isolation alongside men like John McCain. He came home in 1973 — and he never really stopped serving.

Galanti devoted the rest of his life to veterans: advocating for POW/MIA families, working veterans' causes, and reminding America that freedom has a price paid in prison cells as well as on battlefields. He became one of the most beloved figures in the veterans' community, a man whose smile never quite hid what he had survived.

Seven years a prisoner. A lifetime a patriot.

#PaulGalanti #POW #VietnamWar #USNavy #NeverForget

OVER AN HOUR IN 15-FOOT SWELLS. A MASTER EOD TECHNICIAN SAVED FIVE DROWNING AIRMEN IN A RAGING SEA.

Explosive Ordnance Disposal technicians are trained to defuse bombs under extreme pressure, but true courage does not stop at the bomb suit.

While stationed in Turkey, Senior Master Sergeant Riemer was on a morale boat trip in the Aegean Sea when a sudden, violent storm erupted. Gale-force winds and churning 15-foot swells pushed the vessel away from a group of airmen who were swimming toward a nearby island, leaving them stranded in open water.

Seeing panic set in, Riemer plunged off the deck into the maelstrom. In near-zero visibility, he fought relentless currents for thirty grueling minutes to pull two drowning airmen back to the boat. Looking across the churning water, he spotted three more airmen clinging to each other as their strength failed. Disregarding his own exhaustion, Riemer grabbed flotation devices and dove into the raging waves a second time, secured a safety line around the trio, and hauled all three aboard.

Over an hour in the water, Riemer single-handedly pulled five lives from the sea. When asked about his thoughts during the chaos, he calmly said, “I was thinking I’m an EOD technician, and EOD technicians solve complex problems.”

According to official reporting from DVIDS, Riemer was presented with the Airman's Medal for his heroic actions.

A combat-tested leader who holds the distinction of being the first EOD technician in military history to earn the Military Freefall Jumpmaster Badge, Senior Master Sgt. Riemer proved that the warrior mindset shows up whenever lives are on the line.

On August 5, 1964, Lieutenant Everett Alvarez's A-4 went down over North Vietnam — making him the first American naval aviator captured in the Vietnam War. He was twenty-six years old. He would not see freedom for eight and a half years.

Alvarez endured some of the longest continuous captivity of any American POW: years of isolation, torture, and uncertainty in camps across North Vietnam. He resisted, he survived, and he came home in 1973 with his dignity intact.

The war lasted a decade for America. For Everett Alvarez, it lasted 3,113 days — and he never gave his captors what they wanted most: his spirit.

#EverettAlvarez #POW #VietnamWar #USNavy #NeverForget

A Green Beret posts up and returns fire while a local fighter beside him covers his ear against the noise. One man is locked in on the fight. The other is finding out just how loud it gets when the shooting starts.

Working alongside partner forces is at the heart of what Special Forces do, and moments like this show the difference experience makes. Some people talk tough. Others stay steady and keep their rounds on target when it's actually happening.

Everyone wants to be a gangster until it's time to do gangster shit.

“SHOT IN THE HELMET AND ARM, HE RIGGED WEBBING TO LOWER FOUR PARALYZED TEAMMATES DOWN A 60-FOOT CLIFF.”

On April 6, 2008, during the Battle of Shok Valley in the rugged Nuristan Province of Afghanistan, Special Forces Operational Detachment Alpha 3336 (ODA 3336, 3rd Special Forces Group) walked into an ambush of catastrophic proportions.

Over 200 entrenched enemy fighters held the high ground on terraced cliffs, raining down relentless machine-gun, sniper, and RPG fire. The assault element was trapped on a narrow, 100-foot ridge, taking catastrophic casualties.

Down at the base of the mountain, Special Forces Medical Sergeant Ronald J. Shurer II didn’t hesitate. Under heavy fire, he charged up the steep, snow-covered rocky incline to reach his pinned-down teammates.

What followed across the next six hours stands as one of the greatest feats of combat medicine in American military history:

 While treating a critically wounded commando, an enemy sniper round struck the back of Shurer’s helmet with concussive force. He shook off the impact and continued treating casualties until another bullet struck his arm. Ignoring his own wounds, he refused to stop.

Shurer stabilized multiple Green Berets and Afghan Commandos who had suffered catastrophic trauma, including severed limbs, traumatic brain injuries, and paralysis, all while exposed on the sheer face of the mountain.

Facing imminent encirclement, Shurer rigged nylon tubular webbing around rocks and trees. Under direct enemy fire, he manually lowered four paralyzed and critically injured teammates down a 60-foot near-vertical cliff, using his own body as a physical shield to deflect incoming rounds and falling rock debris.

Shurer then helped carry the wounded across a freezing, raging river to the medevac landing zone, continuing to treat patients until every man was evacuated. Because of his actions, not a single American died on that mountain.

President Donald J. Trump presented Ronald J. Shurer II with the Medal of Honor on October 1, 2018.

After leaving the Army, Shurer continued his service to the nation as a Special Agent on the U.S. Secret Service Counter Assault Team (CAT). In May 2020, he tragically passed away from stage 4 lung cancer at the age of 41, leaving behind his wife Miranda and two young sons.

A true Green Beret. A warrior medic. An American hero.

On October 26, 1967, Lieutenant Commander John McCain's A-4 was shot down over Hanoi. He ejected with two broken arms and a shattered leg, was bayoneted by his captors, and spent the next five and a half years as a POW in the infamous "Hanoi Hilton."

When the North Vietnamese discovered his father was an admiral, they offered him early release — a propaganda prize. McCain refused, honoring the POW code: first in, first out. He endured years more of torture rather than leave his fellow prisoners behind.

He came home in 1973 and served his country for the rest of his life. But it was in that cell, refusing to break, that John McCain showed who he was.

#JohnMcCain #POW #VietnamWar #USNavy #NeverForget

A French soldier during Operation Synapse in Kapisa Province, Afghanistan, on March 6, 2010. From March 1 to 7 that year, French troops from Task Force Lafayette, partnered with the Afghan National Army, carried out the operation in the province, which led to a new post being established in the Tagab Valley.

Kapisa and neighboring Surobi, just east of Kabul, were France's area of responsibility during those years. The roughly 2,200 strong Task Force Lafayette became operational there in November 2009, and its soldiers spent the following years fighting in the province's rugged valleys, often in close contact with the insurgency. Building outposts like the one in Tagab was part of the effort to extend security and push the Afghan state's presence deeper into the region.

More than 70,000 French soldiers served in Afghanistan between 2001 and 2014.

Looks like nobody’s getting those “FREE $5,000” checks after all. I’m starting to think mine got lost in the mail—along with all those promises to lower my bills.

The worst part? I’d already spent that imaginary $5,000 at least three different ways. Now I’m supposed to go back to living like it never existed?

Daniel "Chappie" James began as a Tuskegee Airman, flying P-51s in the last months of World War II. He kept climbing — through Korea, through Vietnam, where he commanded air power as deputy commander of 7th Air Force — until, in 1975, he became the first Black four-star general in American history.

James was as famous for his words as his wings: a fierce, eloquent patriot who believed in America enough to demand it live up to itself. In Vietnam, his leadership helped shape the air campaign; at home, his example helped shape the nation.

From Tuskegee to four stars — a journey measured not just in rank, but in the doors he opened behind him.

#ChappieJames #TuskegeeAirman #VietnamWar #USAF #NeverForget

HISTORY IN THE PACIFIC: The U.S. Navy has deployed its first operational drone warship alongside a Carrier Strike Group.

In a major milestone for naval warfare, the Theodore Roosevelt Carrier Strike Group got underway in the Pacific accompanied by the Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel (MUSV) Seahawk—marking the first time an autonomous robotic warship has deployed operationally with a frontline carrier strike force.

What this means for the fleet:

• The Platform: Seahawk is a 145-ton trimaran drone ship engineered to navigate open ocean autonomously for months at a time, requiring zero crew aboard.

• The Mission: Operating miles ahead of the strike group, autonomous surface vessels act as forward radar pickets, electronic warfare nodes, and anti-submarine tracking scouts—detecting threats long before they enter missile range of the carrier.

• The Pacific Strategy: As peer threats expand long-range anti-ship missile arsenals across the Indo-Pacific, pairing manned supercarriers and destroyers with expendable, sensor-packed unmanned vessels is the Navy's primary answer to distributed maritime operations.

Seeing sailors watch a robotic warship trail off the fantail is a surreal glimpse into the future of naval combat.

Would you trust autonomous drone ships to hold the line in a high-intensity naval fight, or does human instinct on the bridge remain irreplaceable?

On February 6, 1967, Airman First Class Duane Hackney — a pararescueman, a PJ — was lowered into a jungle clearing in Vietnam to rescue a downed pilot. Enemy f*re was tearing through the trees. Hackney went in anyway, again and again, pulling men from burning wreckage while rounds cracked past him.

For his actions that day and across his service, Hackney received the Air Force Cross and became the most decorated enlisted airman in American history. PJs live by a creed: "That others may live." Hackney didn't just recite it. He bled for it.

When everything is on the line and the helicopter can't stay, the PJ goes down the cable. Duane Hackney was the best of them.

#DuaneHackney #Pararescue #VietnamWar #USAF #NeverForget

Master Sgt. Fred Baker, Air Force Combat Controller. Combat Controllers are special operations forces and certified air traffic controllers. They deploy into hostile and austere environments, often alongside other special operations teams, to establish airfields, control aircraft, and bring air power to bear. Their motto sums it up: "First There."

Baker's career in the field goes back years. In 2005, as a Senior Airman with the 21st Special Tactics Squadron at Pope Air Force Base, he was named the Air Force Combat Control Airman of the Year. Among the work recognized that year, he directed the delivery of humanitarian relief supplies to impoverished schools reopening after years of tyrannical oppression.

It's a reminder that the skills Combat Controllers bring to the battlefield don't only deliver firepower. They can also deliver hope.

In September 1965, Lieutenant Colonel Robinson Risner was leading one of the war's boldest air strikes when his F-105 was shot down over North Vietnam. What followed was more than seven years as a POW — years of torture, isolation, and resistance in which Risner, as a senior officer, held his fellow prisoners together.

Before his capture, Risner had already become a legend: a Korean War ace who volunteered for Vietnam and flew some of the most dangerous missions of the air war. In captivity, his courage took a quieter form — refusing to break, keeping faith, leading from inside a cell.

He came home in 1973 with his honor intact and his spirit unbroken. Twice awarded the Air Force Cross, he remains one of the greats of American air power.

#RobinsonRisner #POW #VietnamWar #USAF #NeverForget

The warning comes as two Iranian officials confirmed to The New York Times that Tehran has expanded its target list to include American diplomats and personnel prompting the U.S. to cut non-essential embassy staffing and heighten force protection across the theater (i24NEWS, Ground News).

After nearly 60 years, the Vietnam-era Hueys that have served the Washington, D.C., area are starting to retire, and their replacement has just arrived.

In an early-November ceremony at Joint Base Andrews, the first of 26 HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopters touched down, flown straight from Sikorsky's plant in Connecticut. It is the first new rotary-wing aircraft to call the D.C. area home in almost six decades.

The upgrade is significant. Compared with the aging UH-1N Huey, the Jolly Green II has a larger airframe, carries far more fuel, flies faster and farther, and offers about three times the airlift capability. And unlike the Hueys' blue, white, and gold paint, the new aircraft will stay gray.

"This mission deserves the modern capability and safety upgrades that are available today," said Col. Karl W. Seekamp, who called the transition a "monumental milestone."

The handover will take years, with full operational capability expected by 2030. But after 60 years, a new chapter has begun.

Honoring the life and ultimate sacrifice of Brian Ray Hoke—former U.S. Navy SEAL officer and paramilitary operative with the CIA’s elite Special Activities Center (Ground Branch).

A 1996 graduate of the U.S. Naval Academy and BUD/S Class 212, Hoke served with distinction at SEAL Team 3 before continuing his service on the front lines of global counterterrorism with the Central Intelligence Agency.

On October 21, 2016, Hoke gave his life while leading an assault against an ISIS-Khorasan (ISIS-K) stronghold near Jalalabad, Nangarhar Province, Afghanistan. For his extraordinary valor under fire, he was posthumously awarded the Intelligence Star and is memorialized with an anonymous star carved into the CIA Memorial Wall in Langley, Virginia.

"Never above you. Never below you. Always beside you." Fair winds and following seas, Brian.

From 1965 to 1967, Lieutenant General Lewis Walt commanded every Marine in Vietnam — III Marine Amphibious Force — during the hardest years of the buildup. A decorated World War II and Korea veteran, Walt believed the war would be decided in the villages, and he pushed his Marines to protect the population as fiercely as they fought the enemy.

Under his command, the Marines pioneered pacification efforts that became models studied for decades. Walt never pretended the war was simple. He just insisted it be fought with both courage and conscience.

He led the Corps' largest combat command through its trial by fire, and he never asked his Marines to do anything he wouldn't do himself.

#LewisWalt #USMC #VietnamWar #IIIMAF #NeverForget

“BY 2030, POLAND WILL FIELD MORE TANKS THAN GERMANY, FRANCE, ITALY, AND BRITAIN COMBINED.”

While much of Western Europe spent the post-Cold War decades downsizing heavy armor divisions, Poland a nation of 38 million is executing the most ambitious conventional military buildup on the European continent.

By the end of the decade, the Polish Land Forces are projected to field an active arsenal of over 1,500 modern main battle tanks. For comparison, the combined tank fleets of the United Kingdom (~150), France (~220), Germany (~300), and Italy (~200) total fewer than 900 vehicles.

Key pillars behind Poland’s armored juggernaut:

Warsaw has acquired 366 U.S. Abrams tanks, including 250 factory-fresh M1A2 SEPv3 variants and 116 upgraded M1A1 FEP models to anchor heavy mechanized divisions along the eastern border.

A landmark agreement secures 1,000 K2 Black Panther tanks, consisting of 180 initial deliveries and 820 K2PL variants co-produced in Polish factories with localized reactive armor and active protection systems.

 Poland leads the entire NATO alliance in defense investment, dedicating over 4% of its GDP to military procurement and readiness.

The tank buildup is integrated with 96 Boeing AH-64E Apache Guardian attack helicopters, hundreds of HIMARS and K239 Chunmoo rocket launchers, and F-35A Lightning II stealth fighters.

 Poland is actively scaling its armed forces toward a target of 300,000 personnel, cementing its status as NATO’s primary conventional land bulwark on the Eastern Flank.

The center of gravity in European defense has permanently shifted east from the Rhine to the Vistula.

Chief Special Warfare Operator (SEAL) Kevin A. Houston grew up in West Hyannisport, Massachusetts, on Cape Cod, and graduated from Barnstable High School in 1994. He enlisted in the Navy in January 1995 and completed SEAL training in 1999, beginning a career that took him through SEAL Team 4 and eventually to DEVGRU, the Navy's Special Mission Unit.

On August 6, 2011, during his fourth tour in Afghanistan, Houston was aboard the CH-47 Chinook known as Extortion 17 when it was shot down in Wardak Province. The helicopter was carrying a quick reaction force to reinforce Army Rangers already engaged on the ground. All 38 people on board were killed, including 30 Americans, making it the single greatest loss of life in Naval Special Warfare history.

He was 35 years old. Friends remembered him as kind, outgoing, and tougher than anyone around him, and his mother said he was born to be a SEAL. He left behind his wife, Meiling, and their three children.

Lieutenant General Victor "Brute" Krulak saw the Vietnam War more clearly than almost anyone in Washington — and paid the price for saying so. It's one of the most improbable images in the history of air combat: one fighter jet, over enemy territory, physically pushing another crippled jet through the sky to keep it flying. It really happened, on March 10, 1967, over North Vietnam, and it's remembered as Pardo's Push.

He and his backseater were about to go down deep in enemy territory. His wingman, Captain Bob Pardo, refused to let that happen.

Pardo had Aman lower his tailhook, the steel hook used to catch wires on a carrier, then eased it against the glass of his own windshield and began to push. Aman shut down his engines. For about 20 minutes, one Phantom flew two, the hook slipping off every few seconds, Pardo repositioning and pushing again, until he'd driven the dying jet some 80 miles into Laos. Then his own engine caught fire and he ejected too.

All four men were rescued within two hours. Pardo's reward at first was a reprimand for risking the aircraft. It took 22 years before he got the Silver Star. He never called it heroism, he just refused to leave his wingman behind.

“EVIDENCE INDICATES PARTS OF THE JET BROKE OFF BEFORE IMPACT.” — Federal investigators with the National Transportation Safety Board reveal that the doomed Learjet 60 that crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, likely suffered an in-flight structural breakup at altitude, aligning with dashcam video appearing to show the aircraft plunging nose-first without its T-tail horizontal stabilizer.

Aerodynamic & Forensic Breakdown
The In-Flight Breakup Finding: During their initial media briefing in Palm Beach County, NTSB investigators confirmed that the Learjet 60 began shedding components prior to striking the ground, officially expanding the search radius across residential neighborhoods miles away from the primary impact crater.

The Missing Horizontal Stabilizer: Close-up frame analysis of civilian dashcam footage captured seconds before impact appears to show the aircraft's T-tail fuselage cleanly sheared off, missing the entire horizontal stabilizer and elevator assembly that controls aircraft pitch.

Why Loss of the Stabilizer is Fatal: On swept-wing, T-tail jets like the Learjet 60, the horizontal stabilizer generates continuous downward aerodynamic force to counter the natural forward center of gravity. If the stabilizer separates due to severe structural flutter, pitch trim runaway, or aerodynamic over-stress, the aircraft immediately lawn-darts into a near-vertical terminal dive that is physically impossible to pull out of, regardless of pilot yoke input.

The Escalating Mayday Telemetry: Flight tracking telemetry and ATC recordings show the crew encountered severe weather and icing while climbing through 8,700 feet. The aircraft suddenly entered an uncontrollable overspeed condition, with vertical descent rates accelerating from 10,000 FPM past 32,000 FPM before the violent ground collision.

Key Investigation Priorities for the NTSB
Locating the Empennage Components: Ground teams are prioritizing the recovery of tail structure fragments, elevator control horns, and pitch trim actuators to determine whether failure was aerodynamic, mechanical, or structural.

Analyzing Trim Jackscrew Position: Recovery crews will inspect the horizontal stabilizer trim actuator jackscrew to determine if an uncommanded runaway pitch condition preceded the structural separation.

Evaluating Atmospheric Stress & Icing: Meteorologists and investigators are analyzing weather radar data to evaluate whether severe convective turbulence or structural ice accumulation induced catastrophic aerodynamic loading at cruise altitude.

“WE’RE GOING TO CRASH INTO THE GROUND! WE’RE OUT OF TIME!”  Chilling final cockpit recordings emerge as federal investigators identify 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha as the co-pilot aboard the doomed Learjet 60 that plunged over 32,000 feet per minute into Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board.

“We’re going to crash into the ground! ... We’re going to die! Holy f***, we’re out of time!”

Frenzied cockpit audio broadcast over Air Traffic Control frequencies seconds before ground impact

Key Details from the Crash Investigation
The Catastrophic Descent: Flight tracking data released by Flightradar24 indicates the twin-engine Learjet 60 (tail number N722BD) had departed South Florida en route to the Bahamas when it suddenly rolled past 60 degrees of bank and entered an uncontrolled vertical dive exceeding 32,000 feet per minute, erupting into a massive fireball upon impact in a roadway near Lantana.

Co-Pilot Identified: Officials and family members confirmed the first officer was 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha, an aspiring commercial aviator who fell in love with flying as a teenager, earning her private pilot’s license at age 17 while still attending high school before advancing through commercial multi-engine ratings.

All Nine Aboard Perished: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed that both flight crew members and all seven passengers were killed instantly in the high-speed impact and resulting explosion. No ground fatalities were reported despite the crash occurring adjacent to commercial buildings.

NTSB and FAA Launching Full Probe: Specialized go-teams from the National Transportation Safety Board have secured the wreckage site to recover the cockpit voice recorder (CVR), inspect flight control surface actuators for mechanical jam or pitch runaway, and analyze engine thrust settings.

Technical Investigation Priorities
Assessing Sudden Loss of Control: Investigators are focusing on whether the high-performance business jet experienced trim runaway, structural failure, wake turbulence encounter, or an unrecoverable aerodynamic stall at cruising altitude.

Analyzing High-Altitude Flight Dynamics: The extreme reported descent rate of 32,000 FPM suggests the airframe was in a near-vertical terminal dive, pointing toward catastrophic system failure or total loss of pitch authority.

Crew Experience and Type Rating Review: The NTSB will examine pilot rest logs, aircraft maintenance records, and total turbine time in type for both flight deck crew members. 

RIP Nathalia Gadelha and the other members aboard.

Prisoners of war have tried everything to escape, but few plans were as patient — or as strange — as Benjamin Purcell's. Held in a North Vietnamese prison camp, the Army officer spent months secretly drilling tiny holes into his cell door, a little at a time, always watching for the guards. His early-warning system was a chicken he had trained to react whenever anyone approached.

On December 7, 1969, he slipped through the opening and spent nearly ten hours outside the wire — he even caught a bicycle ride toward Hanoi — before being recaptured and thrown into stocks for two weeks. He would not see freedom until 1973. He retired as a colonel, carrying one of the most remarkable escape stories of the Vietnam War: no tools, no help, just patience, nerve, and a chicken.
